title: Unified Inference Governance and Runtime Contract ADR
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This ADR defines a unified governance contract and technical controls that bind API behavior, runtime guarantees, cost-safety mechanisms, and observability requirements across Redwood Inference deployment modes (hosted, Dedicated, Private). Its goal is to create a single source of truth for what production inference services must provide to callers, SREs, and downstream billing/analytics systems.

Context and motivation

We operate multiple serving runtimes (hosted inference, Dedicated GPU pools, private runtime-sidecars). Historically teams have relied on inconsistent expectations for latency, failover, cost signals, and telemetry. This led to three classes of problems: degraded customer experience during capacity transitions, opaque cost allocation, and delayed detection of quality regressions when models or quantization profiles change. This ADR prescribes a governance layer that enforces:

- A machine-readable runtime contract that accompanies every model and route.
- Runtime enforcers for cost and latency safety (circuit breakers, early-exit triggers, and model-fallbacks).
- Standardized telemetry and SLO set emitted by every service (request, token, model-version dimensions).

Decision

We adopt a unified, declarative runtime contract format ("inference-contract-v1") and the following governance pattern:

1) Contract artifact: every model artifact in the model-registry must be accompanied by inference-contract-v1.yaml. The contract contains: service-level SLOs, cost and latency budget, supported API surface (sync/streaming, early-exit), compatibility hints (accepts-seed, deterministic-tokenization), and allowed quantization tiers.

2) Contract validation: a CI gate (contract-validator) enforces schema, minimum SLOs, mandatory telemetry hooks, and a cost budget annotation before a model can be promoted to production or to a Dedicated pool.

3) Runtime enforcement: the runtime-orchestrator and inference-gateway read contracts at deploy time. They enforce contracts via guardrails: request-priority tagging, soft/strict circuit-breakers, early-exit thresholds, and automatic fallback routing to an approved variant if a contract violation is detected.

4) Observability obligations: every request must emit the following minimal dimensions: request_id, tenant_id, model_id, model_version, variant_id, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, inference_time_ms. Aggregated SLIs are computed at 1m and 5m windows and exported to telemetry-collector.

5) Cost & budget flow: billing-proxy reads token counts and maps them to cost profiles attached to the contract. If a tenant or route exceeds its real-time budget window (see policy below), requests are throttled with a 429 and labeled with cost_budget_exceeded for audit.

Rationale

- Declarative contracts let us reason about model guarantees independent of runtime implementation and make automated validation and enforcement possible.
- Guardrails at the gateway provide deterministic behavior for callers during overload or model-quality regressions.
- Embedding cost budgets into contracts makes cost-control observable and actionable at deploy time rather than reactive in billing reports.

Contract schema (high level)

Example snippet (human readable):

---
model_id: rdx-bert-sim-1
model_version: v2024-03-12
service_guarantees:
  p50_latency_ms: 60
  p95_latency_ms: 300
  error_rate_p95_window: 0.001
cost_profile:
  token_cost_usd_per_1000: 0.0025
  daily_budget_usd: 1000
  burst_budget_tokens: 200000
compatibility:
  supports_streaming: true
  deterministic_tokenization: true
  allowed_quantization_tiers: [fp16, int8q4]

Operational controls and thresholds

The following table summarizes the minimum enforcement thresholds that all contracts must include. Teams may tighten these thresholds for a particular route.

| Dimension | Minimum enforced value | Enforcement action | Owner service |
|-----------|------------------------|--------------------|---------------|
| p95 latency | <= 500 ms (hosted), <= 700 ms (dedicated) | soft-shed then strict-fallback | inference-gateway |
| error rate | <= 0.005 (0.5%) | route failover to fallback-variant | runtime-orchestrator |
| cost burn | daily budget annotation required | real-time throttle + audit | billing-proxy |
| telemetry lag | <= 60s ingestion delay | auto-alert to obs-oncall | telemetry-collector |

Runbook: contract violation detection and remediation

1) Detection
   - telemetry-collector computes rolling SLIs and emits contract_violation events when thresholds are breached for > 2 consecutive 1m windows.
2) Automated remediation (first line)
   - inference-gateway attempts a soft fallback to a pre-approved variant (same contract family) while preserving 10% traffic to primary for sampling.
   - If cost budget triggered, billing-proxy returns 429 with guidance header X-Redwood-Cost-Advice containing current burn-rate and recommended model-variant.
3) Escalation
   - If remediation fails after 90s or error rates continue > threshold, oncall is paged using the incident channel with runbook link.
4) Post-incident
   - Runbook owner opens a triage doc under regression-triage and schedules a root-cause analysis within 3 business days.

Rollout plan

- Phase 1 (1 month): contract schema rollout to model-registry and integration of contract-validator in the CI for all model onboarding PRs.
- Phase 2 (2 months): inference-gateway reads contracts in staging and begins enforcement of telemetry hooks and p95 latency scoring (non-blocking).
- Phase 3 (3 months): enable strict enforcement and cost-budget throttles for new routes; migrate top 20 tenants to enforced contracts.
- Phase 4 (ongoing): adopt contracts for Private deployments via runtime-sidecar contract agent.

Alternatives considered

- Option A: Lightweight runtime annotations without a schema — rejected because it lacked validation guarantees and made automatic enforcement brittle.
- Option B: Rely solely on post-deploy observability and SLO alerting — rejected because remediation is slower and customers experience visible failures.

Implications and follow-ups

- Engineering work required: contract-validator service, runtime binding in runtime-orchestrator, billing-proxy real-time enforcement hooks, telemetry-collector contract_violation pipeline. Estimated 4-6 sprint effort across infra and serving teams.
- Product policy: product must expose contract configuration in the Console (readable and editable with RBAC).
- Security: contracts will sometimes carry allowed-quantization-tiers; access to modify contracts requires platform-admin role and audit logs.

Ownership and maintenance

- Policy owner: eng-platform (maintains schema and console surface).
- Runtime enforcement owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Observability owner: eng-platform-observability.
- Billing & cost owner: finance-engineering.

Open questions

- Should contracts include explicit quality delta thresholds (semantic regression budgets) tied to eval harness? (action: coordinate with applied-ml-and-evals team, due 2024-04-01)
- How to represent multi-tenant shared GPU pool budgets more precisely? (action: eng-sre to propose pool-level budget model by 2024-05-15)

Decision status

This ADR is approved and effective for all new model promotions. Existing production models must submit a migration plan within 60 days.
